classify.v4/fragment.instructions: Is the person's new message an incomplete piece that only makes sense together with their previous message?

criteria.true: It adds to or finishes the previous message (for example "and the tests too"), and read alone its meaning is unclear.

classify.v4/kind.instructions: What is the person's new message, in relation to the conversation so far?

criteria.new_ask: It asks for new work that does not continue the previous exchange.
criteria.follow_up: It continues the previous exchange: more detail, a next step, or a related question.
criteria.correction: It says the last reply or the work was wrong, or it changes what was asked.
criteria.control: It tells the assistant to stop, pause, wait, carry on, or change how it works, rather than asking for work.
criteria.addressed_to_task: It is meant for one of the live tasks listed in the state, not for this conversation.
criteria.social: It is a greeting, thanks, or small talk that asks for no work.
criteria.other: None of the kinds above fits.

classify.v4/mentions_other_conversation.instructions: Does the person's new message refer to a different conversation, channel, or session than this one?

criteria.true: It points at something said or done elsewhere (for example "what we discussed in the other channel").
criteria.false: It refers only to this conversation, or to nothing earlier at all.

classify.v4/offer_task.instructions: Does this message describe work to be done later, in more than one step, that the person has not asked to start now?

criteria.true: The person says what should happen later or lists things to do ("we should…", "later can you…", "next: a, b, c"), and nothing in the message asks for that work to begin in this conversation.
criteria.false: The message asks for something now, is a question, is chat, or describes a single quick step.

classify.v4/scope.instructions: Is the person's new message about one line of work, or does it ask about everything going on in this place across the live threads?

criteria.thread: It is about one line of work, or about nothing that spans the listed threads.
criteria.place: It asks across all the work going on here: what else is under way, the state of everything, or the other lines of work beside this one.

classify.v4/should_promote.instructions: Should the work this message asks for run as a separate background task rather than inside the conversation?

criteria.true: The work is long or slow, can go on without the person watching, and the person would not want to wait in the conversation for it.
criteria.false: The work is quick, needs back-and-forth with the person, or the message asks for no work.

classify.v4/thread.instructions: A cue at the start of a message that names a point of view or a voice picks how the answer is said, not which line of work it belongs to. Which of the live threads, if any, is the person's new message about?

criteria.pr-round: The thread «tarnlib PR round», whose goal is: Land the tarnlib PR once review passes. (it works on tarnlib, PR_DESCRIPTION.md).
criteria.pipeline: The thread «datatidy pipeline», whose goal is: Keep the nightly datatidy report right. (it works on datatidy, report.py).
criteria.homesvc: The thread «home server chores», whose goal is: Keep homesvc patched. (it works on homesvc).
criteria.new_thread: The message starts a new line of work that none of the listed threads covers, and that will take more than this one exchange.
criteria.home: The message is a one-off, small talk, or about nothing the listed threads cover: it belongs in the ordinary conversation.

classify.v4/wants_fresh_look.instructions: Does the person want the assistant to set the conversation so far aside and start over?

criteria.true: The message asks to start fresh, to forget the earlier discussion, or to look at the problem anew.
criteria.false: The message builds on the conversation so far.
